content: The following individuals and organizations contributed significantly to the development of the 2019 WHO Consolidated Guidelines on HIV Testing Services (HTS): 1. Key Contributors: Duard Sanders (KEMRI-Wellcome Trust, Kenya) Tanya Shewchuk (Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, USA) Stephen Stafford (Shout-It-Now, South Africa) Joanne Stekler (University of Washington, USA) Christian Stillson (Clinton Health Access Initiative, USA) Anne Sullivan (National Health Service, UK) Weiming Tang and Joseph Tucker (University of North Carolina Project–China, China) Ouk Vichea (National Centre for HIV/AIDS, Dermatology and STD, Cambodia) Anthony Vautier (Solthis, Senegal) Samantha Westrop (National Health Service and Public Health England, UK) Ingrid Wilson (University of Washington, USA) Leo Wilton (Department of Human Development, State University of New York, USA) William Wong (University of Hong Kong, China, Hong Kong SAR) Liu Yan (Consultation Center of AIDS Aid and Health Service, China) Lycias Zembe (UNAIDS, Switzerland) 2. WHO Steering Committee and Core Team: Rachel Baggaley, Cheryl Johnson, Magdalena Barr-DiChiara, Muhammad Jamil, Arshad Altaf, and Allison Wringe (Department of HIV) Anita Sands (Regulation and Prequalification Department) Melanie Taylor (Reproductive Health Research) Fatim Cham Jallow (WHO Regional Office for Africa) Van Thi Thuy Nguyen (WHO Vietnam) Elena Vovc (WHO Regional Office for Europe) 3. WHO Guideline Steering Group Members: Annabel Baddeley, Anne Brink, Michel Beusenberg, Fabio Caldas de Mesquita, Lastone Chitembo, Shona Dalal, Maeve Brito De Mello, Philippa Easterbrook, Nathan Paul Ford, Mary Eluned Gaffield, Joumana Hermez, Oluwafunke Ilesanmi, Naoko Ishikawa, Bhavin Jani, Mark Lanigan, David Lowrance, Frank Lule, Simbarashe Mabaya, Virginia Macdonald, Antons Mozalevskis, Busisiwe Msimanga-Radebe, Oyuntungalag Namjilsuren, Morkor Newman Owiredu, Ena Oghenekaro Oru, Anne-Laure Page, Martina Penazzato, Maria Mercedes Perez Gonzalez, Irena Prat, Vimlesh Purohit, Giovanni Ravasi, Bharat Rewari, Michelle Rodolph, Ahmed Sabry, Julia Lynn Samuelson, Anita Sands, Nicole Seguy, Mukta Sharma, Satvinder Singh, Annette Verster, Lara Vojnov, and Teodora Wi. 4. WHO Staff and Consultants: Special thanks to Rachel Baggaley, Cheryl Johnson, Muhammad Jamil, Anita Sands, Magdalena Barr-DiChiara, Caitlin Quinn, Carmen Figueroa, Niklas Luhmann, and Bradley Mathers for their contributions to writing, coordination, and research. 5. Virtual Working Group on HTS: Special acknowledgment to Valerie Delpech (Public Health England, UK) for her contributions to the forthcoming 2020 WHO Consolidated HIV Strategic Information Guidelines. 6. Additional Contributors: Beth Barr (United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Kenya) Lenhe Dube (Ministry of Health, Eswatini) Buhle Ncube (WHO Consultant, Zimbabwe) Lynne Wilkinson (International AIDS Society, South Africa) 7. WHO Administrative and Technical Support: Administrative support was provided by Valerie Amiel Fourtas, Belen Dinku, and Veronique Millot. Technical support was provided by Robert Benou and Laurent Poulain. Communication support was provided by Oyuntungalag Namjilsuren. Editing was conducted by Ward Rinehart and Sarah Johnson (Jura Editorial Services), with additional support from Bandana Malhotra, Mary Henderson, and Vicky Rossi. Design and layout were managed by L’IV Com Sarl. 8. WHO Guideline Review Committee: Special thanks to Marion Blacker, Susan Norris, Olympe Peretz, and Rebecca Thomas Bosco for their review and input. 9. Overall Coordination: Cheryl Johnson and Rachel Baggaley coordinated the guideline development process under the supervision of Andrew Ball (WHO Department of HIV, STIs, and Global Hepatitis Programme). The guidelines aim to consolidate existing and new recommendations on HIV testing services, addressing emerging evidence and issues since the release of the 2015 and 2016 guidelines. They emphasize the importance of early treatment initiation, prevention strategies, and reaching key populations such as men who have sex with men, people who inject drugs, sex workers, transgender individuals, and those in closed settings like prisons. The guidelines also provide operational guidance on demand creation, testing strategies, and resource optimization to achieve global and national HIV targets.
